analyst.summary: Indian Oil looks statistically cheap (about 4.7x trailing earnings, below book value) but FY26's record Rs 36,802 crore profit was a peak-cycle number - boosted by a refining-margin spike, inventory gains, and a one-off government compensation catch-up that together will not repeat. In fact the reversal has already started: industry marketing margins on petrol and diesel have swung sharply negative in the current (Apr-Jun 2026) quarter because global crude jumped on Middle East tensions while domestic pump prices stayed flat, a repeat of the same government-pricing pattern that hurt IOC's earnings in FY23 and FY25. Debt is genuinely coming down and the dividend is generous, but with no real revenue growth (down slightly over the last three years) and a structural risk of the government capping retail prices in bad crude quarters, we don't think the current valuation is the bargain it appears to be. We rate it a Sell.
